specificForms.titleEn: As an Ordinary Finite Verb Phrase
specificForms.titleZh: 作為一般限定動詞短語
specificForms.descriptionEn: The simple past is natural when the sentence describes a completed period of great happiness. The simple present is possible for repeated situations, although the progressive form is generally more common for a current emotional state.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 簡單過去式適合描述一段已經結束的極度喜悅。 簡單現在式可以用於反覆出現的情況，但描述目前的情緒狀態時，進行式通常更加常見。

benefits.en: The idiomatic version presents the happiness as powerful, light and almost physically uplifting.
benefits.zh: 慣用語版本把喜悅描寫得十分強烈，令人彷彿身體也變得輕盈。

benefits.titleEn: It Connects Good News with an Emotional Result
benefits.titleZh: 把好消息與情緒結果連繫起來
benefits.en: The structure clearly connects one event with the emotional state it produced.
benefits.zh: 這個句式清楚連繫一件事情及其所造成的情緒狀態。

benefits.en: The perfect progressive makes it possible to show that the feeling continued beyond the original event.
benefits.zh: 完成進行式可以表示這份喜悅在事件發生後仍然持續。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful When Reacting to Good News
benefits.en: This is a natural and warm response when somebody shares important good news.
benefits.zh: 當別人分享重要喜訊時，這是一種自然且親切的回應方式。

benefits.en: The expression can describe not only present happiness but also possible or expected future happiness.
benefits.zh: 這個表達不只可以描述目前的喜悅，還可以描述可能或預期出現的未來喜悅。

benefits.en: The image suggests that a person feels so light and happy that normal walking no longer seems possible. The expression is vivid, but it is not automatically better than very happy or delighted in every situation.
benefits.zh: 這個畫面令人想像某人高興得身體也變得輕盈，彷彿已不再踏在地面上。 這個表達十分生動，但並非在所有情況下都一定比 very happy 或 delighted 更好。

origin.statusEn: Gradual Metaphorical Development; Exact Origin Unknown
origin.statusZh: 逐漸形成的比喻；確切來源不明

history.en: The exact first use of walk on air has not been firmly identified. Historical idiom references generally place the established expression in the late nineteenth century. An earlier related image appears in nineteenth-century writing through wording such as tread upon the air, but this should not be presented as the proven first use of the exact modern idiom.
history.zh: walk on air 的確切首次用法尚未能確認。 歷史慣用語資料一般指出，這個固定表達在十九世紀後期已經形成。 十九世紀較早期的作品亦出現過 tread upon the air 等相關意象，但不應把它當成現代慣用語 walk on air 的已證實首次用法。

history.en: The expression compares intense happiness with physical lightness or floating. When people feel delighted, they may describe themselves as feeling lifted, weightless or hardly connected to the ground. Walk on air packages that emotional image into a short verb phrase. Dictionary.com likewise describes the expression as a metaphor comparing great happiness with floating.
history.zh: 這個表達把極度喜悅與身體輕盈或飄浮的感覺作比較。 當人們欣喜若狂時，可能會形容自己彷彿被托起、失去重量，甚至雙腳不再接觸地面。 walk on air 把這個情緒畫面濃縮成一個簡短的動詞短語。

origin.memoryEn: Great happiness makes the person feel light; in the idiom, that person becomes so light that they seem able to walk on air.
origin.memoryZh: 強烈的喜悅令人感到身體輕盈；在這個慣用語的畫面中，某人甚至輕得彷彿能在空中行走。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：on air 必須保持不變
rules.zh: on air 必須保持不變

rules.titleZh: 規則二：只改變 walk，不改變 on air
rules.zh: 只改變 walk，不改變 on air

rules.titleZh: 規則三：進行式必須使用 be

rules.titleEn: Use It Only for Strong Happiness
rules.titleZh: 規則四：只用於強烈的喜悅
rules.en: The ordinary situation does not normally justify such a strong expression.
rules.zh: 她在全國比賽中勝出，欣喜若狂。 她找到一隻乾淨杯子，便欣喜若狂。 一般情況並不足以支持如此強烈的表達。

examples.en: She won the national competition and was walking on air.
examples.zh: 她在全國比賽中勝出，欣喜若狂。

examples.en: She found a clean cup and was walking on air. ✗
examples.zh: 她找到一隻乾淨杯子，便欣喜若狂。

rules.titleEn: Preserve the Cause of the Happiness
rules.titleZh: 規則五：保留令人高興的原因
rules.en: The shorter answer is grammatical, but it removes the important situation supplied by the source.
rules.zh: 較短的答案在文法上正確，但刪除了原句所提供的重要情境。

rules.titleZh: 規則六：保留時間及持續期
rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a continuing state into a completed past state.
rules.zh: 錯誤答案把持續至今的狀態，改成了已結束的過去狀態。

rules.titleZh: 規則七：保留可能性及條件
rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a future possibility into a present fact.
rules.zh: 錯誤答案把未來的可能性變成了現在的事實。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “On Air”
rules.titleZh: 規則八：不要與 on air 混淆
rules.en: On air can mean that a television or radio programme is being broadcast. The interview is on air now.
rules.zh: on air 可以表示電視或電台節目正在播放。 訪問現在正在播出。 這個意思與 walk on air 無關。

rules.titleEn: Avoid Literal Fantasy or Physical Meanings
rules.titleZh: 規則九：避免使用奇幻或物理上的字面意思
rules.en: Only the second sentence uses the emotional idiom taught in this exercise.
rules.zh: 魔法鞋令英雄可以在空中行走。 英雄拯救村莊後欣喜若狂。 只有第二句使用了本練習所教授的情緒慣用語。

examples.en: The magical shoes allowed the hero to walk on air.
examples.zh: 魔法鞋令英雄可以在空中行走。

examples.en: The hero was walking on air after saving the village.
examples.zh: 英雄拯救村莊後欣喜若狂。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Mild Relief Alone
rules.titleZh: 規則十：不要單純用於輕微的鬆一口氣
rules.en: The expression may include relief when the relief produces great happiness.
rules.zh: 如果安心的消息同時帶來強烈喜悅，便可以使用這個表達。 一家人得知治療奏效後欣喜若狂。 我找到自己的筆後欣喜若狂。

examples.en: The family was walking on air after hearing that the treatment had worked.
examples.zh: 一家人得知治療奏效後欣喜若狂。

examples.en: I found my pen and was walking on air. ✗
examples.zh: 我找到自己的筆後欣喜若狂。
